_comment: The why-now layer. Each trigger maps to an Intradiem angle, the personas it routes to, and a 'stakes' line that turns the trigger into a closing window: why acting now beats acting later. The stakes line is what makes a busy exec move their calendar.

wfm_hiring.label: Hiring WFM / RTA / workforce staff
wfm_hiring.play: They are solving intraday with headcount. Lead with automate-versus-hire math before the roles fill.
wfm_hiring.stakes: Once those reqs close, that cost locks into your run-rate, and the new heads won't recover the idle time they're meant to cover. It's far cheaper to fix before the offers go out.

cc_expansion.label: Contact center or market expansion
cc_expansion.play: Volume is scaling. Best time to add automation is during expansion, before headcount locks in.
cc_expansion.stakes: A ramp is exactly when idle time and coaching gaps peak. Fix it after the classes are trained and you've already paid for both.

cost_mandate.label: Cost reduction or efficiency mandate
cost_mandate.play: Direct ROI story. Recover idle labor cost already on the payroll.
cost_mandate.stakes: That target is due this fiscal period, and this is recoverable cost you can book now, without a transformation project or new headcount.

leadership_change.label: New operations or CX leader
leadership_change.play: New exec wants an early, measurable win. Offer a fast ROI proof.
leadership_change.stakes: Your first 90 days is when you can still pick the win, and recoverable labor cost is the fastest one on the floor.

csat_pressure.label: CSAT, AHT, or service-quality pressure
csat_pressure.play: Coaching delivered in idle time lifts quality without adding to the schedule.
csat_pressure.stakes: Every month it slips, agents churn and CSAT compounds downward, and both get more expensive to claw back.

qbp_earnings_pressure.label: Stars/QBP financial pressure disclosed
qbp_earnings_pressure.play: Lead with the parent's own disclosed number, then localize: 'your own guidance names Stars as the headwind; contract [ID] is forgoing an est. $[X]M/yr, and $[Y]M of that gap sits in the CAHPS, complaints, appeals, and customer-service measures our platform acts on.' Route the QBP dollar column from the universe file as the personalization variable.
qbp_earnings_pressure.stakes: Parent has publicly committed capital or guidance to fixing Stars, so budget and executive attention exist now; the cost of waiting is another full ratings cycle of forgone bonus, and the disclosure itself is the prospect's language, not ours.

quality_identity_gap.label: Public quality identity contradicts sub-4.0 CS score
quality_identity_gap.play: The account publicly markets itself on quality or service (state 5-star rating, US News award, brand-as-experience) while its CMS customer-service Star sits below 4.0. Mirror their own language back: 'you lead publicly on quality, and the gap to the 4.0 bonus on [contract] is sitting almost entirely in the CAHPS, complaints, appeals, and customer-service measures, which is the exact part that contradicts the brand.' Personalize on the addressable dollar plus their own public quality claim.
quality_identity_gap.stakes: The gap between the public quality brand and the CS score is a reputational and a revenue exposure at once; every cycle it persists, the marketing promise and the CMS scorecard diverge further and the forgone bonus compounds.

verint_backoffice.label: Verint back-office tool in use [field intel: users often dissatisfied]
verint_backoffice.play: Displacement wedge. They already bought the category and the incumbent is underdelivering; lead with what real-time orchestration does that a clunky reporting layer cannot.
verint_backoffice.stakes: Every renewal cycle that passes locks another year of shelfware spend, and the backlog discipline it was bought for still is not there.
verint_backoffice._source: Nate, Aug 18 2026 tooling call: Verint back-office users he has spoken with are unhappy; NICE usually bundled free with front office and harder to displace.

web_product.label: Read a product or platform page on intradiem.com
web_product.play: They are reading the product, not the category. Lead with the page's use case as a question they are already asking, never with the visit itself.
web_product.stakes: Teams that go looking for orchestration are usually a budget cycle away from picking something. The cost of a slow answer is a shortlist you are not on.

web_proof.label: Read a customer story, ROI, or webinar page
web_proof.play: They want evidence. Open with the peer outcome closest to their vertical and let the number do the asking.
web_proof.stakes: Proof is what a champion carries into a budget conversation. Get it into their hands before that meeting, not after.

web_return.label: Returned to the site inside 7 days (per session, capped at 3)
web_return.play: Repeat visits mean an internal conversation is underway. Offer the thing that shortens it: a working session, not a deck.
web_return.stakes: Each return visit without a conversation is a week they spend building the case with someone else's material.

web_from_us.label: Came to the site from our own email or LinkedIn ad
web_from_us.play: The sequence is working. The next touch references the topic they clicked through on and moves to a specific ask.
web_from_us.stakes: Attention from an outbound touch decays in days. The follow-up has to land while the click is still fresh.

web_content.label: Read blog or thought-leadership content only
web_content.play: Top of funnel. Keep them in the ads audience; no direct outreach on this alone.
web_content.stakes: Content readers are early. The window is to be the name they associate with the topic before a vendor search starts, not to pitch.

lemlist_click.label: Clicked a link in a lemlist sequence
lemlist_click.play: They opened the door a crack. The next touch names the asset they clicked and asks one question about it.
lemlist_click.stakes: A click without a follow-up inside 48 hours reads as automated. Reply speed is the signal they are judging.

lemlist_reply.label: Replied to a lemlist sequence
lemlist_reply.play: Reply triage owns the response. This trigger exists so the account's heat and lane reflect a live conversation.
lemlist_reply.stakes: A reply is the warmest signal the engine sees. Every hour without a human answer hands the conversation back to their inbox queue.

webinar_registered.label: Registered for an Intradiem webinar
webinar_registered.play: They raised a hand to marketing. Sequence copy references the webinar topic, never the registration.
webinar_registered.stakes: Webinar interest fades inside a month. The follow-up belongs in the same fortnight as the session.

webinar_attended.label: Attended an Intradiem webinar
webinar_attended.play: They gave us an hour. Open with the one point from the session most relevant to their function and ask what they'd want to see live.
webinar_attended.stakes: Attendees who do not hear from a person inside two weeks file the session under 'content' and move on.

li_engaged.label: Reacted to or commented on an Intradiem LinkedIn post
li_engaged.play: They raised a hand in public. Open with the post they engaged with and one question about how that topic shows up in their operation.
li_engaged.stakes: Post engagement is a seven-day window. After that the post is gone from their feed and the reference reads as surveillance instead of attention.
li_engaged._note: Person-level. Written by the Clay workflow 'LI Post Engagement' onto people fields Clay Person Signal / Date / Source; the heat scorer folds it in at the person's company domain. Cheaper than a product-page read by design (12 vs 30).

sf_activity.label: Salesforce deal or activity state changed
sf_activity.play: The CRM already knows this account. Open from the last real conversation on record, not from zero, and ask what changed since.
sf_activity.stakes: A closed-lost account that hears nothing for a year is a new-logo pursuit again. Inside six to eighteen months it is still a conversation that paused.

detail_subtypes.closed_lost_aged: Closed-lost 6 to 24 months ago, no open deal. Re-engage lane.
detail_subtypes.open_deal_moved: Open deal updated inside 14 days. HOLD for cold lanes; the AE owns it.
detail_subtypes.renewal_120d: Customer with a deal closing inside 120 days. customer_am lane only.
detail_subtypes.customer_quiet_90d: Customer with no deal update in 90 days. Risk flag to the AM, never a cold touch.

sf_activity._note: Company-level, read from Audiences segments 'SF Activity: *' (deal predicates rooted at companies). Subtypes ride in the trigger detail; the lane rules in heat_loop.json decide who may act, the weight only says how warm.

_recency_note: Per-trigger 'recency' overrides the global block (web and engagement families decay faster than market triggers). Engine merges: global recency, then the trigger's own keys.
